requirement: An immutable parcel record that validates weight and dimensions when constructed, computes a billable weight as the larger of actual and volumetric weight, keeps that value out of the constructor, and gives each parcel its own tag list.
skeleton: Frozen slotted Parcel dataclass with a default_factory tag list, an init=False billable field, and __post_init__ validation that sets it through object.__setattr__.
caption: A frozen standard-library dataclass for shipping parcels that validates itself and derives a billable weight once. The module defines VOLUMETRIC_DIVISOR as 5000 and MAX_WEIGHT_KG as 70.0. Parcel is declared with dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) and has weight_kg, length_cm, width_cm and height_cm fields, a tags list created per instance with field(default_factory=list), and a billable_kg float declared with field(init=False) so callers cannot pass it. __post_init__ raises ValueError about the weight unless it is greater than zero and at most MAX_WEIGHT_KG, so the limit itself is allowed, and raises ValueError about the dimensions when any of them is zero or negative. It then computes the volume, divides it by VOLUMETRIC_DIVISOR to get the volumetric weight, rounds the larger of the actual and volumetric weights to two places, and stores it with object.__setattr__ because a frozen instance rejects normal assignment. The fixture asserts that a 2 kg parcel of 50 by 40 by 30 bills 12.0, that a dense 10 kg parcel bills 10.0, that 70.0 is accepted while 0.0 and 70.01 raise ValueError, that a zero dimension raises ValueError, that assigning weight_kg raises FrozenInstanceError and passing a billable value raises TypeError, and that appending a tag to one parcel leaves a new parcel's tags empty.

plan.intent: Build an immutable parcel that validates itself and derives its billable weight
constraints: Weight must be above zero and at most 70 kg, otherwise ValueError
Billable weight is the larger of actual and volume divided by 5000, rounded to two places
Billable weight is not a constructor argument and the record is frozen
Each parcel gets its own tag list

rationale.teaches: A frozen dataclass that validates in __post_init__, fills an init=False field with object.__setattr__, and uses default_factory for mutable defaults.
rationale.why: Validation that sits in a factory function is skipped by anyone who calls the class directly, and a derived field that callers can pass can disagree with its inputs. Constructing parcels at the boundaries shows whether the limits and the derivation hold.

ops.docstring: Validate a frozen parcel record at construction and derive its billable weight.

ops.source:
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Parcel:
    """An immutable parcel whose billable weight is fixed at construction."""

    weight_kg: float
    length_cm: int
    width_cm: int
    height_cm: int
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    billable_kg: float = field(init=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not 0 < self.weight_kg <= MAX_WEIGHT_KG:
            raise ValueError(f"weight must be in (0, {MAX_WEIGHT_KG}] kg")
        if min(self.length_cm, self.width_cm, self.height_cm) <= 0:
            raise ValueError("dimensions must be positive")
        volume = self.length_cm * self.width_cm * self.height_cm
        volumetric = volume / VOLUMETRIC_DIVISOR
        billable = round(max(self.weight_kg, volumetric), 2)
        object.__setattr__(self, "billable_kg", billable)

candidates.why_wrong: A parcel with a zero dimension is accepted and billed by its actual weight alone.
A parcel at exactly the 70 kg limit is rejected.
Every parcel built without tags shares one list, so a tag added to one appears on the next.
The volumetric divisor is 6000, so bulky parcels are under-billed.
The smaller of the two weights is billed, so bulky and dense parcels are both under-charged.
